<!-- Provide a more detailed description of the PR, other things fixed or any additional comments/features here -->
## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

Adds caching to the plugin results for 1 day per query, using the LazyCache library. Returns cached results in initial Query() call, otherwise queries OneNote itself in the delayedExecution:true call.

<!-- Describe how you validated the behavior. Add automated tests wherever possible, but list manual validation steps taken as well -->
## Validation Steps Performed

(with win32 OneNote installed) Run PowerLauncher, and in the dialog type "o:", then press enter on a result to open it in OneNote. Or you can run the runner, and then enable the OneNote plugin in the UI and do the above. If you query OneNote, the first time there will be some lag (~1s) since it's querying OneNote, but if you run the same query a second time, the results should be virtually instantaneous

issue_context.title: PT Run OneNote plugin should use temporary caching to speed up successive queries
issue_context.body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Currently the plugin queries OneNote every time, which on my local instance takes about 900ms with 3 pretty decently sized notebooks. We can add in memory caching to store a list of results by query and only update it once a day, or even less. Perhaps if the plugin is specified explicitly (o: prefix) then it bypasses the cache, but for global queries uses it.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Any time a global query is run with the OneNote plugin enabled

### Supporting information

_No response_
comments: Do you call the query of onenote data every time whe results are requested?
Yes, see the first line of the issue :)

It might ne an idea to query only frome onenite if last data wuery was before mire than x second. This will lead to the behavior that the plugin only queries the onenote data on the start of the search query and not on each letter input. 

I implemented this for the net adapter information in the system plugin.

Hmm, do you mean to use the DelayedExecution overload? If so, good idea! I submitted a PR which adds per-result-caching using LazyCache, and returns cached results during `Query(..., false)`, and uncached results during `Query(..., true)`

> Hmm, do you mean to use the DelayedExecution overload? If so, good idea! I submitted a PR which adds per-result-caching using LazyCache, and returns cached results during `Query(..., false)`, and uncached results during `Query(..., true)`

I mean doing something like this: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Microsoft.PowerToys.Run.Plugin.System/Components/Commands.cs#L161-L167. (Not sure if it has changed with implement the throttle in PT Run. But before each typed character executes a search with querying the data source.)

I see, but I'm not sure how that would work. If the user types "s", then we'd cache all the pages that contain "s", but then they type "leep" but we'd still be showing all the different pages that merely contain "s", until 5 seconds have elapsed AND they type something else, right? That doesn't seem very useful. In your case it works because the IP list isn't unique per query, right?

> I see, but I'm not sure how that would work. If the user types "s", then we'd cache all the pages that contain "s", but then they type "leep" but we'd still be showing all the different pages that merely contain "s", until 5 seconds have elapsed AND they type something else, right? That doesn't seem very useful. In your case it works because the IP list isn't unique per query, right?

Yes the network interface data are unique. Can you get all pages without filtering from the one note api?

I worry about strange results with your way of caching.
**Example:** First you search "a" and see the page "ab note". Then you delete "ab note". If you then search for "a" you see "ab note" from cache and the result disappear when you have typed "ab" because it isn't in the list return from the one note api for the query "ab". This might confuse the user.

Why not caching `OneNoteProvider.PageItems` and doing the search in the plugin itself?

Yes you can get all pages, but that's a lot of data to cache. In my case for example that's 502 pages, and I think about 16MB of content. Either way of caching would yield the same behavior in your "ab note" example, that's just an unavoidable side-effect of caching, whether caching the results or the pages themselves.
